fix(macapp): stop the History pane's invalidation storm (WORKROOM-2B App Hang)

Sentry WORKROOM-2B reported a >=2000 ms App Hang whose main-thread sample landed in
HistoryRow.body -> AvatarSubject.gravatar -> String(format:) -> __CFStringAppendFormatCore.
The format string was only where the sample happened to land. Three factors multiplied:

1. HistoryRow, DivergentSiblingRow and ChangesPanel.ChangedFileRow each held
   @EnvironmentObject AppStore + @ObservedObject TerminalSessions purely to answer "is my
   commit/file the focused tab?" — one string comparison. TerminalSessions republishes on
   every terminal title write and activity pulse, so while an agent streamed, EVERY row
   body re-ran at OSC frequency.
2. HistoryPanel's list was an eager VStack, so every loaded row was built on- or off-screen.
3. The window was unbounded: loadMore grew it 100 at a time and refresh re-read the whole
   grown prefix on every ref write.

Measured on the pre-fix code, then after (WorkroomAppTests/HistoryRowInvalidationTests):

  one 25-pulse burst, 60 commits ....... 60 row bodies -> 0
  200-commit page, first render ........ 400 row bodies -> 8
  200-commit page, first layout ........ 406 ms -> 35 ms  (so ~1000 rows was the 2 s hang)

Changes:
- New Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift resolves the focused tab's identity ONCE per panel body
  pass; HistoryPanel and ChangesPanel own the TerminalSessions dependency and hand rows plain
  values. No inspector row observes an ObservableObject for selection any more. This also
  replaces three copies of the same store+sessions guard chain.
- Equatable + .equatable() on HistoryRow, HistoryRootRow, DivergentSiblingRow and
  ChangedFileRow. `open:` is excluded from == and made behaviour-constant (static title
  helper + explicit [store] capture) so the exclusion is sound.
- HistoryPanel's list becomes a LazyVStack. Safe here and not in DiffViewer: these rows are
  fixed-height, so the height estimate a lazy stack caches is correct. Both comments now say
  which property decides that.
- Rows take an explicit themeGeneration. Their token reads sit inside ternaries, so an
  unselected, unhovered row registers no Observation dependency; it used to repaint only
  because applying a theme also republished TerminalSessions. Caught by a test, not by eye.
- Avatar hex encoding replaces 16 Foundation format-string parses per author with a nibble
  table, byte-identical to %02x (pinned for all 256 values plus RFC 1321 anchors). Deletes
  the unused GhosttyApp.hexColor, the only other String(format:) outside a view body.
- HistoryModel caps the window at 1000 commits (injectable), clamping loadMore and refresh,
  with a "Showing the newest 1,000 commits" notice in place of a dead "Load more". This
  bounds the per-ref-write read, which is one commit decode per row of the window.
- AvatarImageFailures remembers URLs whose load failed so lazily-rebuilt rows stop
  re-requesting missing Gravatars; cleared on app activation, because AsyncImage's failure
  phase carries no HTTP status and an offline scroll must not blank avatars until relaunch.

Observability (why the report was unreadable): nightly.yml never installed sentry-cli and
passed no SENTRY_* secrets, so release.sh's dSYM upload silently skipped every night — hence
three unnamed app frames. Nightly now installs it in its own tolerant step (an unattended
cron must lose symbols, never the build), passes the secrets, and release.sh annotates the
run summary on success as well as on skip. SentryConfig reports the Nightly build as
environment "nightly" instead of "production".

Tests: HistoryRowInvalidationTests + ChangedFileRowInvalidationTests (pulse burst rebuilds
nothing; selection, content and theme changes still do; lazy realization; a wall-clock
ceiling), FocusedTabSelectionTests, SentryConfigTests, HistoryModelTests window-cap cases,
hex equivalence in AvatarSubjectTests, and HistoryStressUITests (800-commit fixture via
-WorkroomUITestManyCommits: realized rows far below the model, 2 s interactivity budget,
scroll-recycle and offscreen-selection cases). HistoryPushStateUITests now selects rows by
commit short id instead of by position, because offscreen lazy rows leave the a11y tree.

Deferred to TODOS.md with context: a status-aware avatar loader, FilesPanel's 4000-row eager
list (measure first), and main-thread timing from a real hang.

Done, committed on `joel/history-hang-fix` (not pushed).

**Root cause fixed.** Three row types (`HistoryRow`, `DivergentSiblingRow`, `ChangedFileRow`) each held `@EnvironmentObject AppStore` + `@ObservedObject TerminalSessions` to answer one string comparison. `TerminalSessions` republishes per terminal title write and activity pulse, so every row body re-ran at OSC frequency, over an eager `VStack`, over an unbounded window. The `String(format:)` in the Sentry sample was the leaf, not the cause.

**Measured, before → after** (`HistoryRowInvalidationTests`, red on `master` first):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 25-pulse burst, 60 commits | 60 row bodies | **0** |
| 200-commit page, first render | 400 row bodies | **8** |
| 200-commit page, first layout | 406 ms | **35 ms** |

406 ms for 200 rows is the arithmetic that made ~1000 rows a 2-second hang. The diagnosis is now measured, not inferred.

**Two things the process caught that I had wrong:**
1. My first Changes-panel test passed vacuously (fixture lacked `lastChecked`, so the panel rendered "Checking…" and drew no rows). The positive-half assertion is what exposed it; both suites now carry anti-vacuity guards. Same class of bug hit the first stress-UI guard, which asserted on "Load more" — a button that legitimately isn't realized below 800 lazy rows.
2. A real regression I introduced: rows read `theme.tokens` only inside ternaries, so an unselected, unhovered row registers no Observation dependency. Pre-fix they repainted only because applying a theme also republished `TerminalSessions`. Removing that observation removed the accidental repaint. Fixed with an explicit `themeGeneration` input, asserted by test in both panels rather than eyeballed.

**Verification run:** `make app-format`, `make app-lint` clean; full unit suite 1753/1754 (the one is `testDiagnosisQuality`, a pre-existing eval gated behind `/tmp/workroom-run-agent-eval`); XCUITest `HistoryStressUITests`, `HistoryPushStateUITests`, `ChangesetDetailUITests`, `ChangesPanelUITests`, `InspectorAnimationUITests` all pass.

**Not done, deliberately:** the Instruments pass. The numbers above plus the 2-second XCUITest interactivity budget answer the causality question it was there to answer, and its output needs GUI inspection to be worth anything. Say the word if you want it anyway. The nightly dSYM upload can only be confirmed by the next nightly run: look for a `::notice::` line for the upload, and new events tagged `environment: nightly`.

**User-visible changes to know about:** history stops at 1000 commits with a "Showing the newest 1,000 commits" note; History rows' accessibility label now leads with the commit short id (VoiceOver reads it, and UI tests select by it instead of by position).

3	/// UI test for the activity bar's **Changes dirty dot**. The fixture (`-WorkroomUITestFixture 1`)
4	/// auto-selects the jj fixture workroom, whose seeded `WorkroomStatus` is `dirty: true`
5	/// (`UITestFixture.workroomStatus`), so on launch the Changes icon must signal the uncommitted
6	/// working tree. The dot itself is decorative (a11y-hidden); the state is announced on the icon
7	/// button's accessibility **value** ("has changes"), which is what this test reads.

13	/// this is excluded from `make app-test` (the unit gate) via a separate scheme.
14	final class ActivityBarDirtyDotUITests: XCTestCase {
15	  override func setUpWithError() throws { continueAfterFailure = false }
16	
17	  private func launchedApp() -> XCUIApplication {
18	    let app = XCUIApplication()
19	    app.launchArguments += ["-WorkroomUITestFixture", "1"]
20	    app.launchArguments += ["-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES"]

29	  }

fix(macapp): unbreak the activity-bar dirty-dot UI test

`ActivityBarDirtyDotUITests` probed `activitySection.history` by name to prove the dirty dot
is Changes-scoped. History left the activity bar in 0fc3b97a (it became a sub-section of the
Changes stack), so `ActivitySection` has only `changes` and `files` and that identifier is
emitted nowhere. Reading `.value` on an element that isn't in the tree throws "Failed to get
matching snapshot", so the test has failed since 2026-07-31 while asserting nothing about the
dot it exists to cover.

Peers are now discovered from the accessibility tree (every `activitySection.*` icon except
Changes) instead of being named, so the next section to join or leave the bar can't silently
break this again — and an empty-peers guard keeps the assertion from passing vacuously if the
query ever finds nothing.

Found by running the full XCUITest suite; unrelated to the WORKROOM-2B work in the previous
commit, which touches no activity-bar file.

Fixed and committed as `8536031b`.

**What changed** (`macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/ActivityBarDirtyDotUITests.swift`): the test no longer names its peer sections. It queries every `activitySection.*` icon in the tree, drops Changes, and asserts none of the rest carries "has changes" — plus an empty-peers guard so the loop can't pass vacuously if the query ever comes back empty. The class doc records why the old version broke, so the next section to move in or out of the bar doesn't repeat it.

Verified: `make app-lint` clean, test passes in 6.8 s.

Full UI suite status is now **176 tests: 175 passing, 1 skipped** — the skip being `DiffHighlightUITests.testRubyDiffIsHighlighted`, which is deliberate and self-documented ("XCUITest can't observe the async-applied highlight a11y value; covered headlessly by `DiffHighlightMapperTests`"). I re-ran only the fixed class, not the whole 28-minute suite; say the word if you want a clean full pass on the record.
